change.title: pr-1-flat
change.description: Enhanced Pagination Performance for High-Volume Audit Logs
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes on every page that has rows (datetime key)
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator` is wired into the audit-log endpoint with `order_by="-datetime"` (src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:79-80). Its `get_item_key` calls `math.ceil`/`math.floor` on `getattr(item, self.key)` (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:839-840), but `AuditLogEntry.datetime` is a `DateTimeField` (src/sentry/models/auditlogentry.py:69). `math.ceil(datetime)` raises TypeError. `build_cursor` calls the key on the first row unconditionally when the cursor has no value (src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:121-122) and on the last row for the next value (src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:137). So any superuser or global-access request with `optimized_pagination=true` that returns at least one audit row gets a 500. Separately, `value_from_cursor` returns the raw millisecond integer (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:842-843), which `build_queryset` binds directly against the datetime column (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:119-126), so page 2+ would also compare a timestamp column with an integer. `DateTimePaginator` (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:233-241) has the correct `get_item_key` and `value_from_cursor`; this class copied the numeric `Paginator` versions instead. The default path is unaffected, but the only new behaviour of this PR fails for its only trigger. Fix: reuse `DateTimePaginator`'s `get_item_key` and `value_from_cursor` (for example, subclass `DateTimePaginator`). No test exercises the branch (see the tests finding).

findings.title: Negative-offset 'advanced' branch raises instead of paging, and its comments are wrong
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code slices the queryset with `queryset[start_offset:stop]` where `start_offset = cursor.offset` (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:880-882). Django's QuerySet rejects negative slice bounds with ValueError ("Negative indexing is not supported."). That premise is Django behaviour and is not in this repository, so I did not read it. If it holds, a superuser who sends a cursor with a negative offset gets a 500, not a page. The comments say the branch 'enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds' and that 'permissions are checked at the queryset level' (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:874-876, 878-879). Neither is true: the queryset is only scoped by `organization_id` (src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:48), and no offset-based access check exists. Cursor offsets are parsed from client input without a sign check (src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:53-59). The sibling paginators reject negative offsets with `BadPaginationError`, which the base view maps to a 400 (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:286-287; src/sentry/api/base.py:540-541). Fix: remove the branch, or reject negative offsets the same way `OffsetPaginator` does.

findings.title: Clamping negative next-cursor offsets silently changes behaviour for every DateTimePaginator endpoint
findings.body: In `BasePaginator.get_result`, the change sets `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182-184). Before the change, `queryset[offset:stop]` ran with the raw offset. Negative slices are rejected by Django (premise not in this repository). So a next-page cursor with a negative offset, such as `1:-5:0` parsed by src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:53-59, used to fail. Now it returns the first page with HTTP 200 and builds the next cursor from that clamped result. This is silent wrong data. It applies to every endpoint that uses `Paginator` or `DateTimePaginator`, because both inherit `BasePaginator.get_result`. The same file rejects negative offsets explicitly in `OffsetPaginator` (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:286-287) and the other paginators (lines 347-351, 700-701, 747-748), so the new behaviour is also inconsistent with the file. The comment at src/sentry/api/paginator.py:179-181 is wrong too: it says negative offsets are allowed, and the claim that 'the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions' is false, since the queryset raises. Nothing in `build_cursor` produces a negative offset, so the clamp only changes results for crafted input. Fix: revert these lines to `stop = offset + limit + extra` and `queryset[offset:stop]`, or raise `BadPaginationError` for negative offsets.

findings.title: `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is dereferenced on every request, even when member is None
findings.body: `enable_advanced` is computed before the `use_optimized` check (line 71), so every GET to this endpoint now evaluates `organization_context.member.has_global_access`. `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is optional (src/sentry/organizations/services/organization/model.py:346). The member is None whenever there is no user id: the organization service only looks up membership when `user_id` is set (src/sentry/organizations/services/organization/impl.py:123-125, 135-140), and `determine_access` passes `user_id=request.user.id` (src/sentry/api/bases/organization.py:285-290). Org-scoped API tokens authenticate as `AnonymousUser()` (src/sentry/api/authentication.py:391), so their member is None. `OrganizationAuditPermission` accepts any request whose access has `org:write` (src/sentry/api/bases/organization.py:93-94, 110-124). If such a token holds `org:write`, the `or` short-circuit does not help (`is_superuser` is False), and the attribute access raises AttributeError. That is a 500 on the default path too, which worked before this change. I have not confirmed that org tokens can hold `org:write`. Fix: read the member only inside the `use_optimized` branch and guard against None, for example `member = organization_context.member; enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or (member is not None and member.has_global_access)`.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator copies BasePaginator.get_result and the Paginator key methods
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:845-911) is a near-verbatim copy of `BasePaginator.get_result` (lines 136-215). The only real difference is the negative-offset branch (lines 877-886). `get_item_key` and `value_from_cursor` (lines 838-843) copy `Paginator` (lines 222-227) and are the wrong ones for a datetime key, which is how the blocker above happened. Two copies of the cursor logic will drift, as the two already have. Prefer subclassing `DateTimePaginator` and overriding only the branch that differs, or removing the class if that branch is dropped.

findings.title: Docstring and comments claim optimizations that the code does not contain
findings.body: The class docstring says the paginator provides 'Streamlined boundary condition handling', an 'Optimized query path for large datasets', and 'backward compatibility' (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:821-832). `get_result` issues the same `queryset[start:stop]` and the same `build_cursor` call as `BasePaginator`, with no different query, index or batching. The apparent intent is also contradicted by the endpoint comments, which call the change a 'Performance optimization for high-volume audit log access patterns' (src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:68-69). The PR body makes the same performance claim, and nothing in the diff measures or changes query cost. Remove the claims, or state what actually differs.

findings.title: Comment says the cursor now allows negative offsets for reverse pagination; the code does not change
findings.body: This file's only change is a comment in `Cursor.__init__` (src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26-27). The code is `self.offset = int(offset)` (line 28), exactly as before. `int()` accepted negative values before this change too, so the comment describes a capability that this PR does not add, and it claims a performance benefit that does not exist. The comment is also misleading about the rest of the PR: the negative-offset paths it refers to either clamp (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182-184) or raise (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:880-882). Remove the comment.

findings.title: The optimized-pagination branch and the new paginator have no tests
findings.body: `tests/sentry/api/endpoints/test_organization_auditlogs.py` is unchanged by this PR and only exercises the default `DateTimePaginator` path. Nothing sends `optimized_pagination=true`, and there is no paginator test for `OptimizedCursorPaginator` or for negative offsets. A single request with one audit row and that flag would have caught the TypeError in the blocker. Add a test that requests the optimized path with rows, and one that checks the negative-offset behaviour you decide on.

The new path uses the numeric Paginator-style key (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:838-843). The query shape is otherwise the same (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:112-126, 897-906).

contracts.action: BasePaginator.get_result clamps negative offsets to 0 for next-page cursors
contracts.equivalent_path: Previously: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182-183 before this change (stop = offset + limit + extra; queryset[offset:stop]). Sibling rejections: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:286-287, 347-351, 700-701, 747-748.
contracts.before_after: Before: a next cursor with negative offset passed the raw offset to queryset slicing. After: next-cursor offsets are clamped to 0. Previous-cursor offsets are still passed raw.
contracts.visible_effect: A crafted next cursor with a negative offset now returns the first page with HTTP 200, and the next cursor is built from that page. This applies to every endpoint that uses Paginator or DateTimePaginator, since both inherit this method.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent wrong page for malformed cursors. Previously the request failed (premise: Django negative slicing). Cursor offsets come from client input (src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:53-59), and build_cursor only adds non-negative amounts.
contracts.open_question: Confirm the Django negative-slice behaviour, as in the previous contract. Confirm which endpoints use Paginator and DateTimePaginator (a search of callers was not run; the list is large).
candidates: grep for DateTimePaginator and Paginator callers under src/sentry/api/endpoints (not run)

summary: The PR's only new behaviour, the `optimized_pagination=true` path, fails for any request that returns rows: `OptimizedCursorPaginator` uses numeric key handling on a datetime column (blocker). Two other changes need fixing: the BasePaginator clamp silently turns negative next-cursor offsets into a first-page response for every DateTimePaginator/Paginator endpoint, and the eager `member.has_global_access` read can 500 org-token requests on the default path (medium confidence). The negative-offset branch raises instead of paging, and several comments and the docstring claim performance or capabilities the code does not provide. No tests were added. The Django negative-slice behaviour that several findings rest on is not in this repository and is marked as an open premise.
